The Nobel Prize in Literature was first awarded on December 10, 1901 [d7][d8], in Stockholm, Sweden [d7]. The recipient was French poet Sully Prudhomme, honored "in special recognition of his poetic composition, which gives evidence of lofty idealism, artistic perfection and a rare combination of the qualities of both heart and intellect" [d4][d6]. This date marked exactly five years after the death of Alfred Nobel, whose will established the prizes [d7][d8]. The Nobel Prize in Literature has since been awarded 117 times to 121 laureates between 1901 and 2024 [d3].
